subject: Post-demo: unit-econ breakdown & next steps on pricing bands
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Simmons <laura@synthhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: unit-econ breakdown & next steps on pricing bands

Hi Laura — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed next steps list so we can get you a pilot price that fits your budget and ROI goals.

Key takeaways (what we heard):
- Primary use case: in-product clinical decision assistant for care coordinators (short multi-turn prompts, average context ~1.5k tokens).
- Expected traffic profile: 200k API calls / month initially, with steady growth to ~600k over 6–12 months.
- User behavior: average tokens per call ~3.5k (prompt + response), peak concurrency modest.
- Budget range from your side: rough target $10k–$25k/mo depending on rollout speed and success metrics.

Quick numbers we need you to confirm:
1) Monthly token volume estimate (all environments): your current estimate was ~700M tokens/month at scale — can you confirm low/expected/high?
2) Pilot length preference: 6 vs 12 weeks (you mentioned procurement prefers shorter trials).
3) Primary success metric for rollout: reduction in time-to-action per case, or NPS uplift with care coordinators?

What we propose next (actions):
- Action A: I attached a lightweight token-econ worksheet — please fill low/expected/high token columns and return. (attachment: synth-token-econ-worksheet.xlsx)
- Action B: Internal unit-econ deep-dive from our infra team to show $/1M tokens sensitivity across quantization/batching profiles — Vivek is looped.
- Action C: If numbers look good, we’ll issue a pilot quote + an SOW (redline term-sheet attached as example).

Initial, back-of-envelope economics we ran on the call (please treat as strawman):
- Target price band requested by you: $200–$350 per 1M tokens.
- With expected fidelity and 8-bit quantization + prefix caching, we estimate production cost to Redwood of $60–$120 per 1M tokens depending on batching and hit-rate for cached prompts.
- That implies contribution margin range ~65%–80% at $350 vs ~40%–70% at $200.

Ben & Vivek — could you pick up with a) a per-feature $/month sketch (based on the usage profile above) and b) 3-month CAC payback scenarios? Laura, once we have your completed worksheet we’ll pin pilot pricing to the low/expected/high buckets.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-demo: unit-econ breakdown & next steps on pricing bands

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline:
- Monthly tokens (low/expected/high): 250M / 520M / 1.1B (we modeled low as limited pilot, expected = 6mo growth, high = full roll).
- Pilot length: procurement prefers 6 weeks but will extend if we see signal early.
- Success metric: percent reduction in average handling time (AHT) per case — target 18% reduction for pilot to justify expansion.

We’ll fill out the attached worksheet and return by EOD Wed. I’m also CC’ing Mike from Finance — he’ll want a clean $/1M token target and a pilot cost ceiling.

Best,
Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Simmons <laura@synthhealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: unit-econ breakdown & next steps on pricing bands

Looping in my quick sketch before Vivek publishes a fuller slice. Two small sanity checks: token mix matters (system vs user vs cached). If synth’s calls are highly templated (many repeated prefixes), cache hit-rate could materially lower marginal cost.

Per-feature sketch (based on Laura's expected bucket = 520M tokens/mo):
- Feature (CI Assistant) calls/month: 520,000 calls
- Avg tokens/call: 3.5k -> monthly token consumption = 1.82B tokens (note: Laura gave tokens for all environments; double-check if 520M was calls or tokens)
- If 520M tokens is the actual tokens number, then calls ~= 150k/month. Need clarification.

Using numbers assuming 520M tokens/month:
- At $/1M tokens price bands: $200 -> monthly spend = $104k; $300 -> $156k.
- Per-feature unit math (if 150k calls/mo): cost per feature invocation (at $300/1M tokens) = (3.5k tokens * $0.0003) = $1.05 per call.

CAC payback (very rough):
- Target CAC per net-new customer: $180
- If feature monetizes as $1.05 per call and average customer uses 20 calls/mo -> revenue/mo = $21 -> payback ~ 8.5 months (too long).
- To hit 3-month payback we need either higher ARPU per customer, lower pricing, or more efficient prompt engineering to reduce tokens/call.

I’ll defer to Vivek for the infra cost sensitivities and a recommended pilot price that leaves room for a healthy margin while hitting Laura’s procurement ceiling.

—Ben

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Simmons <laura@synthhealth.com>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@synthhealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: unit-econ breakdown & next steps on pricing bands

Thanks — I ran a short sensitivity model and exported three scenarios (conservative / expected / optimized). Key levers: quantization mode, batching window, prefix cache hit-rate, and sequence length distribution. I included the attachment we referenced.

Summary (numbers scaled to 1M tokens basis to make comparisons easy):
- Infra cost per 1M tokens (conservative): $125
  - assumptions: fp16, small batching, 10% cache hit
- Infra cost per 1M tokens (expected): $85
  - assumptions: 8-bit quantization, batching 20–30ms, 30% cache hit
- Infra cost per 1M tokens (optimized): $48
  - assumptions: 4-bit/8-bit mixed quant, aggressive batching, 60% cache hit for standard prompts

Translate to $/feature (using Laura's expected: 520M tokens/month -> we assume this is tokens not calls for worst-case):
- If 520M tokens/month and average calls = 150k (3.5k tokens/call):
  - Cost per call (expected infra cost $85/1M): (3.5k / 1M) * $85 = $0.2975 per call
  - If customer charges $1.20 per call (gross), gross margin = ~75% before CAC and other costs.

CAC payback scenarios (assume net-new customer monetizes on the feature only):
- Inputs: CAC = $180; ARPU scenarios based on call frequency: low=10 calls/mo, mid=20 calls/mo, high=40 calls/mo; price per 1M tokens sold = aligned to pilot price.
- Example mid usage at suggested pilot price band ($275/1M tokens -> cost-per-call to customer ≈ (3.5k/1M)*275 = $0.9625):
  - Customer monthly spend (mid): 20 calls * $0.9625 = $19.25 -> payback = 9.4 months.
- To achieve 3-month payback with CAC $180, monthly contribution needs to be $60. That implies either: 62 calls/mo at same price, or a lower price / lower token consumption resulting in higher call volumes per $ spent.

Recommendations (operational):
1) Pilot pricing: offer a stepped pilot with blended price of $220/1M tokens for the 6-week trial, capped at $15k pilot spend. That gives them budget certainty and preserves margin vs expected infra costs (~$85/1M).
2) Prompt engineering quick wins: target reduction from 3.5k -> 2.2k tokens/call via response truncation + structured templates -> ~37% token reduction, improving CAC payback materially.
3) Instrumentation: enable token-level billing reporting per route so we can show real-time pilot economics.

I attached the workbook (synth-token-econ-worksheet.xlsx) with the model and a separate tab showing the three sensitivity slices. If Laura can confirm whether 520M refers to tokens vs calls we’ll run a tailored per-customer scenario.

—Vivek

From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@synthhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: unit-econ breakdown & next steps on pricing bands

Team — thanks for the math and recommendations. Quick clarifications from Finance:
- 520M was intended as expected tokens/month across pilot/dev/prod combined. Calls figure will be lower; I’ll get you the calls estimate by end of day.
- Pilot spend ceiling: Finance is comfortable with $15k cap for a 6-week pilot if we can see instrumentation and a short plan for go/no-go at week 4.

Request: please produce a one-page pilot SOW with: pilot objectives & success metrics (AHT reduction target), capped spend, sample data sharing & security notes, and a single pilot rate (we prefer a flat blended $/1M tokens). Laura & I will route to procurement once we have the SOW + redline term-sheet.

I’ve attached a sample redline we received from procurement; please send a pilot SOW and final pilot price by COB Mon so procurement can fast-track.

Thanks — Mike
